html:
Mauritania is a country in north-west Africa on the Atlantic, nine-tenths of it Sahara desert, with its capital at Nouakchott. It became independent from France in 1960. The map shows its area from 1945, when it was a French colony.

Its land was home to Berber and later Arab tribes. The Almoravid movement began among the desert Sanhaja here in the 1000s, and old caravan towns such as Chinguetti were stops on the trans-Saharan trade. France ruled it as part of French West Africa.

Its first president, Moktar Ould Daddah, built a new capital from almost nothing. In 1975 Mauritania took the southern part of Spanish Sahara, but the war with the Polisario Front went badly, and after a coup in 1978 it gave up its claim. More coups followed. Society is still split between Arab-Berber Moors and Black Africans, and Mauritania was the last country to abolish slavery, in 1981, making it a crime only in 2007.
